subject: Performance SLO / Private VPC - Network qualification follow-up (Acme)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Mar 2028 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Performance SLO / Private VPC - Network qualification follow-up (Acme)

Hi Sam — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and agreed next steps on the performance / SLO side so we have alignment before the network deep-dive: 

Summary of targets we discussed:
- End-to-end inference SLO: 95th percentile request latency <= 350 ms for 512-token responses (sustained QPS goal: 200; burst to 800).
- Streaming requirements: first-byte (initial token) <= 200 ms; steady-state inter-token jitter < 50 ms.
- Concurrency: support up to 500 concurrent sessions during peak, connection re-use preferred.
- Throughput: ability to sustain ~2k tokens/sec aggregate across model fleet for steady-state workloads.

Network / deployment constraints we flagged:
- Private VPC with either AWS PrivateLink or direct peering preferred (no public egress for inference traffic).
- Egress IPs will need to be whitelisted; if NAT is used, please confirm whether static NAT IPs can be provided.
- Internal latency budget: app -> model-host RTT target <= 12 ms (we'll use this as the pass/fail for the perf tests).
- VPN/Peering: BGP peering or Transit Gateway preferred; if you must use site-to-site VPN, please confirm expected jitter and MTU.

Attachments: I included our VPC perf playbook and the perf harness instructions for the test plan.

Next steps (action owners):
- Acme (Sam): share preferred connectivity option (PrivateLink/Direct/Transit) and NAT/egress IP ranges + a contact for netops.
- Redwood (Marissa): schedule 60-min network deep-dive with your network team; provide perf test window options and the test harness runbook.
- Jordan: coordinate test windows and share our lightweight test agent to run inside your VPC (no data leaves the VPC during test).

Can you confirm the connectivity option and share netops contact by EOD Monday? Once we have that we can lock a test slot.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0119
From: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: netops@acme.com
Date: Sat, 03 Mar 2028 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Private VPC - Network qualification follow-up (Acme)

Hi Jordan — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick answers from our side: 

- Connectivity: Acme prefers AWS Direct Connect + Transit Gateway peering for this project. We can provision a private VPC endpoint / PrivateLink if you need it, but primary preference is Direct Connect.
- Egress / NAT: We can provide a static NAT pool for Redwood test traffic; estimating 4 static public IPs for the test cluster. I will confirm exact addresses with netops.
- Internal latency: our internal infra team reports typical app -> us-east-1 model-host RTT ~ 8–10 ms within peered AZs; we should be within the 12 ms target but we'll validate during the test.
- VPN fallback: we can do site-to-site VPN if required, but it has higher jitter; prefer Direct Connect for SLA reasons.

Netops contact: netops@acme.com (cc'd). I also attached a small sample of our recent traceroute+tcpping to the east region (see acme_network_latency_20280228.csv).

Available windows for the network deep-dive next week: Tue 2028-03-07 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed 2028-03-08 14:00–15:00 PT. Let me know which works.

— Sam
Sam Ellis
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Corp
sam.ellis@acme.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@acme.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 04 Mar 2028 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Private VPC - Network qualification follow-up (Acme)

Thanks Sam — great to see Direct Connect as the preferred path (that will give us the most predictable RTT/jitter). A couple of clarifications from the Redwood infra side before the call: 

Technical asks for the deep-dive / test prep:
- Please confirm whether Direct Connect will be full L3 peering to our VPCs or if Traffic will traverse a Transit Gateway (we need the exact topology to size egress/ingress appropriately).
- Confirm MTU on the path (we aim to avoid fragmentation for TLS tunnels).
- Provide the static NAT egress IPs (if NAT is used) so our test agents can target them; if PrivateLink is used instead, provide the endpoint IDs.
- For the perf run we will ask your team to run our lightweight agent inside a test app subnet we specify; the agent performs websocket streaming tests that measure first-token latency and inter-token jitter. Ensure the subnet allows outbound TCP/443 to our test fleet.

Pass/fail criteria we will use during the controlled run:
- First-token latency <= 200 ms (95% of trials)
- Inter-token jitter < 50 ms (95% of trials)
- RTT app -> model-host median <= 12 ms; p95 <= 25 ms
- No >1% connection drops under sustained concurrency at target QPS

I've attached the Redwood VPC perf playbook (redwood-vpc-playbook.pdf) and the perf harness runbook link. Jordan — I can take the lead on the test plan and runbook; Sam, can you confirm Tue 03/07 10:00 PT? If that works we will invite your netops and our infra leads and send a pre-call checklist.

Thanks — Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: netops@acme.com <netops@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Sam Ellis <sam.ellis@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Mar 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Performance SLO / Private VPC - Network qualification follow-up (Acme)

Hi all — netops here. Confirmed: Direct Connect into our Transit Gateway with L3 routing will be used. MTU on the path is 9001 across the dedicated DX link; internal MTU is 1500 in the VPC. We will provide the static NAT IPs by EOD today and have scheduled a 60-min deep-dive on Tue 2028-03-07 10:00–11:00 PT.

Contact for the call: Priya Natarajan (priya.n@acme.com) and myself (netops@acme.com). We'll run initial traceroutes and a short synthetic load during the call to validate baseline RTT.

Attachments: acme_network_latency_20280228.csv

Thanks — Acme NetOps
